payload.name: Preserve explicit motivation for persisting in an activity
payload.description: Use during extraction when a speaker explicitly states what motivates them to keep doing an activity, especially on tough days or through difficulties; include that reason as a distinct fact.
content: During extraction, if a speaker explicitly states the motivation or reason that keeps them doing an activity (e.g., 'knowing X keeps me going even on tough days'), capture that motivation as a separate, explicit detail in the candidate content; do not collapse it into general emotional benefits like escape or healing.
During CRUD, when updating an existing memory, preserve any previously stored explicit motivational facts unless clearly contradicted by the new message; enrich rather than replace them.

solves: Construction extraction candidates often preserve a person's general emotional framing of an activity but omit an explicitly stated reason for persisting through difficulties, causing downstream memory updates to lose that key fact. This skill applies when a speaker explicitly names what keeps them going in an activity; it does not apply to motivations that are only implied or inferable.
